text:
incident-bot: ALERT triggered: p99 latency breach on route /v1/generate in eu-west for service 'inference-api' (window: 5m). Threshold: 1.8s, observed: 3.6s. PagerDuty: pd-12345 fired.

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty incident pd-12345 assigned to Ben (oncall).

Ben (oncall): acked. I'm on it. ETA 5m to triage.

Alice (SRE): noted. Any correlation with KV eviction or recent config rollout? seeing small spike in backend evictions in metrics.

Ben (oncall): looking at pods in eu-west-1: some reallocations around 12:04 UTC. checking autoscaler events.

Carlos (Infra): I pushed a minor scheduler change 20m ago but it was canaryed in a different cluster. not eu-west. I'll grep the kube events for node pressure.

Ben (oncall): top of request path shows tail latency on model-side. KV cache hit rate down from 98% -> 75% over last 10m. probable cache churn.

Alice (SRE): if KV hit rate dropped that fast, maybe a hotkey eviction or large prefix churn. Can we switch route to model-variant fallback (lower mem, higher compute) to relieve memory pressure? runbook suggests fallback route: 
```
# quick reroute
POST /admin/route-replace
{"route":"/v1/generate","target":"variant-coldpath-eu"}
```

Ben (oncall): preparing to flip to variant-coldpath-eu for 2 min to gauge p95 improvement. will announce before execute.

Dana (Support): Customer watchlist: tenant AcmeCorp and FinanceFlow showed uptick in error budgets on dashboards. AcmeCorp has active SLA. Please flag if we expect >5m degradation.

Ben (oncall): flipping now. 

incident-bot: ACTION: route-replace executed by Ben (oncall) at 8312350050.

Ben (oncall): initial numbers: p95 down from 1.9s -> 1.3s, p99 still noisy at 2.6s. KV hit rate recovering to 88%. looks promising.

Alice (SRE): good. monitor CPU on coldpath; it may increase cost, but for now keep for 10m. Also start a targeted cache warmup for top-100 prefixes. I can kick off script.

Carlos (Infra): checking for any node OOMs or eviction logs: none. But I see a surge of long-running batch jobs hitting the same cache shards 12:02-12:07, likely causing thrash. I'll throttle that job queue.

Ben (oncall): throttled queue for batch-retriever. p99 improved to 1.9s after 3m. still above SLO but trending down.

Dana (Support): messaging ready for AcmeCorp: short note "We're investigating elevated latency for inference in eu-west; mitigation in progress. We'll update in 15 minutes." OK to send?

Alice (SRE): yes send that now, include workaround: retry with 200ms jitter if clients see timeout.

Ben (oncall): Sent customer update. Logging actions in incident doc.

incident-bot: NOTE: incident pd-12345 set to "mitigating" by Ben (oncall).

Alice (SRE): plan for next 30m: keep fallback route, run cache warmup job, throttle batch-retriever, observe. If p99 <= 1.6s and steady for 10m, start recovery and revert route to normal staged ramp.

Carlos (Infra): preemptive scaling note: autoscaler shows 30% headroom; we can add 4 nodes if needed. Holding off unless p99 worsens.

Ben (oncall): will hand off at 12:40 UTC to the rotation. leave notes: what we did and current metrics. If p99 climbs >2.5s, escalate to oncall manager.

Dana (Support): queued a follow-up customer update in 12m.

Ben (oncall): handing off to Alice (SRE) for steady-state watch at 12:40 UTC. I'll mark incident as acknowledged and moving to monitoring.

Alice (SRE): taking over watch. tagging incident doc with timeline and commands executed. Will update if any regression.

incident-bot: pd-12345 acknowledged by Ben (oncall), owner transitioned to Alice (SRE).

Ben (oncall): thanks team.

Alice (SRE): rough lessons: unexpected cache-shard contention from batch jobs can cause rapid SLO creep; add a probe to detect KV hit-rate drops and auto-trigger short-lived fallback routing and cache-warmup. I'll file an action item.
